c1-term/c1-total: trap one labels pure inflation as lifestyle creep. c1-prices..c1-total compute what the SAME life costs at an assumed 3% (price_rise), then c1-term calls it lifestyle creep and the c1-total card 'What creep costs' plus the HUD 'Cost of the traps' counts $276,353 as the trap's cost. That cost is inflation, which happens whether or not Rohan spends his raise, so the number does not support the conclusion. Fix: retitle the c1-total card (e.g. 'Same life, 20 years on'), keep it out of the 'Cost of the traps' counter, and say the creep is what comes on top: each raise first has to cover rising prices, and spending the rest is what leaves savings flat.

c3-grows: 'With assumed inflation of 3%, in 10 years his cash grows to only $20,815' is wrong: the cash grows to $20,815 because of the 0.4% interest (the on-screen equation is $20,000 + 0.4% a year), not because of inflation. Fix: 'At 0.4% a year, in 10 years his cash grows to only $20,815.' and move the equation trigger from 'inflation' to a word in the new line.

c3-why: 'Easy-access savings pay little' is not true in general: US high-yield easy-access savings accounts pay a few percent (channel profile: US savings 3-5%). Only the typical big-bank account pays around 0.4%. Fix: 'Many big-bank savings accounts pay this little, because the bank lends that same money out at much higher rates.' and in c3-jar say 'a big-bank savings account'.

c5-year/c5-total: 'that fee is $1,000 every single year, whether the fund does well or badly' (header 'Every year, no matter what') and 'at least $30,000 in fees' are wrong for a percentage fee: 1% of a pot that falls is less than $1,000, and c5-share itself says the fee moves with the pot. Fix c5-year: 'On $100,000, that's $1,000 a year, and the fee is taken whether the fund does well or badly.' (header 'Taken every year'); c5-total: 'Even if the pot never grew, 30 years of it is $30,000 in fees, before counting the growth that money never got to earn.'

c6-sharma: 'The extra years of payments are [the expensive part]' (word overlay 'Years') is false: both mortgages are 360 months (small_months = big_months = 360); the bigger house costs a bigger payment, not more years. Fix: 'The extra payment is, every month for thirty years, and every one comes with a bill.' and change the word overlay to 'Every month'.

recap: 'Spend less than each raise, read the fees, and start early.' tells the viewer what to do with their money in the imperative (rule 4), and the recap equation shows 'Spend less + read fees = Start early'. Fix: 'Rohan's way out: he spends less than each raise, reads the fees, and starts early. So which trap are you in right now? Tell me the number.' Also reframe the payoff rules card (all imperatives: 'Save half of a raise', 'Keep the car longer', 'Beat rising prices', 'Check every fee', 'Buy what you need', 'Start now') as what Rohan does, e.g. 'He saves half of each raise', 'He keeps the car longer', 'He starts now'.
